title: Startup School 2013 office hours: Paul Graham and Sam Altman on launching, markets and founder fit
summary: Live office hours where Paul Graham and Sam Altman question three early startups (a coding game, a progress-video site, a customs brokerage). Recurring themes: don't over-optimize early, test the thing that matters, copy industry defaults, avoid pitching huge markets, and prefer founders who can't stand big-company jobs.

principles.text: Don't over-optimize or wire in an outcome too early; let the product grow into what it becomes and stay empirical.
principles.quote: Don't be don't like like um overoptimize too early. Like let it grow into whatever it's going to grow into.

principles.text: Test the thing that actually matters during beta, such as whether content gets shared and watched, rather than assuming it.
principles.quote: It seems that would have been really important to test during the beta is will people share these on YouTube and do they get watched?

principles.text: Long tenure at a big company counts against a founder; the best founders can't stand it.
principles.quote: if we are looking at some someone's application and they worked for a long time for a large company that's that's actually bad to us because like the the best startup founders probably could not stand that

principles.text: In an unfamiliar industry, use that industry's norms as your default starting point.
principles.quote: whatever they do is probably the the default thing to start with.

principles.text: Huge market numbers hurt credibility with investors; very big markets are bad for startups, not good.
principles.quote: You know, really big markets are bad for startups, not good. Yeah. If you say a too big number, the investors just they just don't believe it, right?

principles.text: If the product is already engaging, stop holding back users for polish; launch and let them spread it.
principles.quote: Well, if it's engaging enough now, you've ironed off out ironed out enough kinks.
